title: The Four Skillful Brothers
text:
A poor man sent his four sons out into the world to learn a trade. After four years they came home. One had become a master thief, one an astronomer, one a huntsman and one a tailor whose magic needle could sew anything.

Their father tested them. The astronomer looked up into a tree and said there was a bird's nest with five eggs at the top. The thief climbed up and took the eggs from under the sitting bird without her noticing. The huntsman set the eggs on a table and broke all five with a single shot. The tailor sewed the shells back together, and when the chicks hatched, each had only a thin red line around its neck.

Soon afterward a dragon carried off the king's daughter, and the king promised her hand to whoever rescued her. The astronomer found her through his telescope, sitting on a rock far out at sea, with the dragon asleep with its head in her lap. The brothers sailed there, and the thief stole her out from under the dragon's head. On the way back the dragon woke and flew after them. The huntsman shot it through the heart, but the falling body smashed their boat. The tailor quickly sewed the planks together, and they all came safely home.

Then they quarreled over who had earned the princess. The king decided that since each had an equal claim, none of them would marry her. Instead he gave each brother a share of his kingdom as a reward.
lesson: Some tasks need every skill on the team, in sequence, and no one can claim the whole success. Arguing over sole credit can cost the prize everyone earned together.
people: Four brothers (a thief, an astronomer, a huntsman, a tailor), a king's daughter, a dragon
source: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 129, The Four Skillful Brothers
